title: agents --update-instructions appends the Quest block without removing the Backlog.md CRITICAL_INSTRUCTION it is meant to replace
description: A workspace migrated off Backlog.md via 'migration backlog apply' predictably still carries the Backlog.md-installer's CRITICAL_INSTRUCTION block in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md ('For every user request in this project, run backlog instructions overview before answering or taking action'). 'quest agents --update-instructions' only appends its own managed Quest block next to that -- it does not detect or remove the Backlog block, even though the migration path it pairs with (quest migration backlog apply) exists specifically to retire that tracker. The result: a session obeying both blocks calls a dead tracker on every turn. 'quest agents --check --require-installed' reports state: current in this exact condition -- it is honest about its own managed block and silent about the contradiction two lines away. Found during the 2026-09-03 five-repo fleet cutover: quest-cli, opum-doc, opum-agent, and opum-cli-e2e all hit this; opum-agent's own report of a clean run turned out to depend on the operator having hand-removed the Backlog block before running the command, which is exactly the shape of a tool whose correct-looking result depends on manual work already done. Scoped to the one competing directive this tool's own migration path guarantees will be present -- the Backlog.md installer's block, which has explicit BACKLOG.MD GUIDELINES START/END markers and needs no prose parsing -- not a general foreign-directive detector.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Running --update-instructions in a workspace that has completed a Backlog migration (or otherwise carries a BACKLOG.MD GUIDELINES START/END-delimited block) either removes that block or leaves --check reporting something other than state: current until it is addressed
If removal is the chosen fix: it is bounded to the delimited BACKLOG.MD GUIDELINES block and does not touch unrelated content
If detection rather than removal is the chosen fix: --check surfaces the contradiction (a distinct state or a validation finding), not state: current
A test exercises a fixture AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md carrying the Backlog block, runs --update-instructions, and asserts the chosen behavior
The command help documents the chosen behavior

implementationNotes:
Fixed with removal (the primary strategy) plus detection (belt-and-suspenders), rather than either alone. A workspace migrated off Backlog.md predictably still carries the Backlog.md CLI installer's own managed block (<!-- BACKLOG.MD GUIDELINES START/END --> markers, confirmed byte-for-byte against this repo's own pre-migration AGENTS.md history) -- agents --update-instructions only ever appended Quest's block next to it, never detecting or removing it, so a session obeying both blocks called a dead tracker on every turn. Chose removal over detection-only because detection-only would have created exactly the same "permanently blocked, needs a manual step" shape QCLI-228 just fixed for version skew -- shifting the burden to a human forever instead of the tool actually fixing what it's meant to fix.

AC1/AC2: checkQuestAgentInstructions now detects the Backlog block's presence (a narrowly-scoped regex matching only the delimited BACKLOG.MD GUIDELINES block, not prose parsing) and reports "drift" even when the Quest block itself is otherwise exact or version-only -- so --check never silently says "current" while the contradiction sits there. applyQuestAgentInstructions strips exactly that delimited block (touching nothing else) as an unconditional final pass over whatever the existing Quest-block logic produces, so removal happens correctly whether the Quest block was missing (the exact fresh-migration shape), already current, or itself drifted -- a compound problem gets fixed in one --update-instructions pass.

AC3: also implemented, on top of removal -- --check surfaces the contradiction as drift rather than reporting current, satisfying this branch too even though removal was the primary fix.

AC4: unit tests (test/integration/agents/local-agent-instructions.test.ts) cover detection alone, detection alongside a version-only difference, removal from all three starting Quest-block states, and bounded removal preserving unrelated authored content on both sides of the block byte-for-byte. CLI-process test (test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts) reproduces the exact fresh-migration shape end to end through the real subprocess: --check --require-installed fails before the fix, --update-instructions removes the block and installs Quest's, --check then reports current, and a separate case confirms drift (not silent current) when only the Backlog block remains beside an already-exact Quest block.

AC5: command help (command-help.ts's "agents" entry) documents the behavior. Full suite 427/427, bun run check green.
finalSummary:
A workspace migrated off Backlog.md predictably still carried the Backlog.md CLI installer's own managed block (BACKLOG.MD GUIDELINES START/END markers), and agents --update-instructions only ever appended Quest's block beside it -- never detecting or removing it -- so a session obeying both blocks called a dead tracker on every turn, and agents --check --require-installed reported state: current the whole time.

Fixed with both removal and detection. checkQuestAgentInstructions now reports drift whenever the Backlog block is present, even if the Quest block is otherwise exact -- --check never silently says current while the contradiction sits there. applyQuestAgentInstructions strips exactly that delimited block (bounded, no prose parsing, nothing else touched) as an unconditional final pass regardless of whether the Quest block was missing, current, or itself drifted, so update-instructions actually fixes the workspace rather than leaving a permanent manual step (the same shape QCLI-228 just fixed for version skew).

Verified against the real Backlog.md installer block, byte-for-byte from this repo's own pre-migration git history. Tested at the library level (all three starting Quest-block states, bounded removal preserving surrounding content) and end to end through the real CLI subprocess (the exact fresh-migration shape). Documented in command help. Full suite 427/427.
